subject: Temporary queueing carve for StormCloud pilot — autoscale waiver request
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@stormcloud.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary queueing carve for StormCloud pilot — autoscale waiver request

Hi team,

Quick background: StormCloud.ai is kicking off a 4-week latency-sensitive pilot next Monday (10/12). Their traffic shape is spiky (short, high-concurrency bursts) and they’ve requested a small carved slice with queueing to avoid cold-start tail latency while we iterate on kernel/quantization tuning.

Ask: Can we grant a temporary queueing carve and an autoscale waiver for the pilot window (10/12–11/08)? Details in the attached stormcloud_pool_plan.xlsx and queueing_config.yaml. What I need from the ops/product side:
- Confirmation we can create a 6-GPU slice (A100x6 equivalent) isolated in the west-us1 pool.
- Temporarily disable the strict autoscale down below 50% utilization for that slice (we prefer soft-eviction instead of preemption).
- Ops runbook for manual eviction/reclaim if overall capacity is needed for higher-priority reserved customers.

Constraints: StormCloud is in the enterprise pilot bucket; they sign an addendum for limited SLA and will accept a higher price while in the carve. They need a 2-hr notice for preemption and prefer routing fallback to a smaller quantized model.

Next step proposal: Kimberly or Marcus to own feasibility + estimated impact on pool headroom by EOD today; Soojin to draft the evict/reclaim runbook; Laura to confirm billing/price uplift for the carve. I’ll coordinate customer comms and can take the DocuSign addendum if legal signs off.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
"On the attachment: stormcloud_pool_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 tabs: forecast, slot-map, costs); queueing_config.yaml (text)"

----

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@stormcloud.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary queueing carve for StormCloud pilot — autoscale waiver request

Neha — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. A few clarifying q's before I sign off:
1) Exact concurrency/lambda per-second numbers during spikes? The spreadsheet has ranges but I need P95/P99 estimates so we can model scheduler impact.
2) Are you expecting any GPU memory pinning or long-lived KV caches per session? That changes slot packing.
3) For the autoscale waiver: do you want no scale-down at all, or a relaxed policy (e.g., min-scale 1 replica per 2 GPUs)?

Prelim thoughts: a 6-GPU carve in west-us1 is feasible if we can re-route low-priority background batch jobs elsewhere. Marcus — can you run a headroom check and show the window where this carve would risk >85% pool utilization? If that hits, we should consider making the carve time-windowed (e.g., 8a–8p) instead of 24/7.

I’ll also need a short note for Billing (Laura) describing the uplift terms to make sure we don’t break pricing rules for reserved customers.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Dedicated Capacity Programs

----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@stormcloud.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 13:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary queueing carve for StormCloud pilot — autoscale waiver request

+1 to the questions. I ran the headroom check against west-us1 pool using current reservations and projected background jobs. Key points:
- Baseline free headroom this week: ~14 GPUs (spread across two racks).
- If we carve 6 GPUs for StormCloud and relax autoscale-down, headroom drops to ~8 GPUs. If we hit a 3-hour sustained peak (rare), the pool utilization could spike to 88–91% and we would need to preempt low-priority reservations.
- Suggested mitigations: window the carve for peak business hours (08:00–20:00 PT) and enable automated fallback routing to the quantized-1 model when preemption triggers.

Runbook notes (short):
- Preemption trigger: pool free headroom < 6 GPUs for > 15m
- Notification: paging to oncall + email to stakeholders (Neha, Kimberly, Laura)
- Eviction behavior: soft-evict StormCloud jobs first; if insufficient, call manual ops to shift batch jobs to secondary region.

I can produce a fuller ops playbook (15–20m) if we greenlight the carve.

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer

----

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@stormcloud.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary queueing carve for StormCloud pilot — autoscale waiver request

We’re aligned to move forward with the carve under the following commitments (summary / action items):
1) Capacity: Marcus to provision 6 GPUs (west-us1) and confirm physical rack placement by 10/09 17:00 PT.
2) Autoscale: Temporary waiver to prevent scale-down below 50% for the slice; Kimberly will approve the exact policy change after Marcus’ headroom dashboard is posted.
3) Runbook: Soojin (me) to author a 1-page eviction/reclaim runbook and post to INF-4321 by 10/09 12:00 PT. It will include preemption triggers, notification steps, and rollback.
4) Billing: Laura to confirm price uplift and addendum wording by 10/09 EOD; Neha will own DocuSign routing.
5) Customer comms: Neha to confirm the 2-hr notice and fallback routing with Marta after we finalize times.

Marta — thanks for the patience; we’ll aim to keep the pilot stable while minimizing risk to other reserved customers. If StormCloud can accept the 08:00–20:00 PT window as a compromise, that reduces risk materially.

I’ll post updates to the Jira ticket and kick off the provisioning once Marcus confirms rack placement.

-Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference

----

For context and attachments: stormcloud_pool_plan.xlsx (forecast, slot-map, cost scenarios) and queueing_config.yaml (suggested queue depth and soft-evict priority).

Onward.
